citations.review_text:
Great short game. The animation work is outstanding, as well as the sound and environment design. Everything on that front is a solid 10/10, and it all builds up to an unsettling but powerful short experience.

My only wish is that there had been a bit more insight into our main character's motives and the reasons behind their actions. The puzzle design also felt a bit repetitive at times. I really liked the game, but I also felt a little empty after finishing it, wishing I knew more about this world that the game never really delved into.

*Actual playtime: 3.5 hours. (Played offline.)

It's really fun and unexpectedly more thrilling than u would expect. The puzzles are at times challenging but somehow intuitive enough to working it out so it finds itself in a delicate balance of challenging but not challenging enough to making it frustrating n not so easy to make it feels like a vain experience. It's just really well made. Only downside is prob the short duration, but the experience kinda offset it so yeah its worth every penny.

note:ik its an old game but I hope for a sequel where u can play co-op.

Here’s my review of the game INSIDE
(no spoilers)

​INSIDE gives you no explanations (really I'm not joking 🫥)

it throws you straight into the game as a little boy in a red shirt trying to escape a mysterious group of people.

Honestly, that’s about all I can say about the plot, because anything more would spoil the experience because the game is too short🥲

​The game heavily focuses on a dark, lonely, and eerie world with minimal story direction. On the gameplay side, however, it’s very straightforward.

It’s packed with clever, brain-bending puzzles, many of which will leave you thinking long after you finish. The audio design is incredibly sharp and immersive. It really feels like the world around you is alive.

​As someone who loves dark and eerie atmospheres, this game was right up my buutycheeks. The graphic content isn't overly intense either. I'd describe the level of gore as pretty mild.

​Graphics: 10/10 ⭐
​Gameplay: 9/10 ⭐
​Sound & Ambience: 10/10 ⭐ (Super Immersive)

​This is a straight ice recommendation from me cuh!😎
You don't expect a platformer with literally no dialog to tell such a powerful story...
Simply amazing. They kept the lore as ambiguous as possible so the player can interpret it for him/herself, much like with LIMBO. Still can't get over the OST, so outstanding.

☐ Not for me

[b]Weighted rating[/b] out of 5
[h3]4.12[/h3]

[h2]Summary[/h2]
Flee through a bleak world, solving environmental puzzles and evading capture.
[b]Best for:[/b] Fans of wordless storytelling, atmosphere, and puzzle-platformers that prioritize mood and environmental narrative.
[b]Skip if:[/b] You dislike narrative opaqueness, or need an explicit plot.

[h1]Review[/h1]
What did I just play? The game launches with no menu, no introduction, no UI elements. Just a boy on the screen who reacts to the controls, and I got moving. The controls themselves are super smooth and intuitive. No fuss, no need for hints; they were just where you expected them to be. The mysterious atmosphere that started this entire experience persisted, and the curiosity about what was going on pulled me back in between sessions. The game was never difficult, but it could be [i]a bit[/i] tricky at times when it came to the puzzles, mostly because of the vast areas.

The art's gorgeous, with muted, dystopian colors. The implementation of light and shadow is brilliant. Sound design is probably one of the best I've experienced, and together with the foreboding soundtrack it adds another layer to the immersive character. Character movements and physics felt refined. And the thoughtful details, like when swimming under the surface there is no UI indication that you're running out of air, just a subtle pulsating vibration on the Deck. Even the [spoiler]shock wave[/spoiler] mechanic felt equally simplistic, beautiful, and deadly. The level design introduced new mechanics at a great pace and mixed moments of urgency with more calm periods. It all just fits so well together.

And to add some meta properties that made this an even better experience: the game saved my location automatically and frequently, making it super easy to continue playing regardless of whether you died or are returning from a previous session. This makes the game feel like it's not pu…

I genuinely feel that INSIDE is one of the best games ever made that you can play in one sitting.
The level design and the visual story (there is no dialogue) are so well meshed, it's AS mind-boggling as the climax of this 3-4 hour experience. 10/10 Masterpiece!

An incredibly atmospheric and mysterious masterpiece.
INSIDE is an absolute work of art. From the very first second to the mind-bending finale, the game grips you with its heavy, haunting atmosphere and never lets go.

What makes this game so brilliant is how incredibly mysterious it is. It doesn't rely on dialogue or cheap exposition to tell its story; instead, it uses visual storytelling, brilliant puzzles, and a dark, clinical art style to pull you into its eerie world. Every screen feels like a carefully crafted painting, and the sound design is remarkably immersive.

It's tense, deeply intriguing, and will leave you thinking about its ending long after the credits roll.

9/10 — A must-play experience that is as beautiful as it is unsettling.

10/10

Inside is a hauntingly brilliant game that proves how powerful storytelling can be without a single line of dialogue. From its unsettling opening moments to its unforgettable finale, every scene is meticulously crafted to build tension, mystery, and intrigue.

The game's minimalist art style and exceptional sound design create an oppressive atmosphere that never lets up. Its puzzles are consistently clever, seamlessly woven into the environment, and always serve the pacing rather than interrupt it. Every new area introduces fresh ideas, ensuring the experience remains engaging from beginning to end.

Inside is a masterpiece of visual storytelling and game design. An unforgettable experience that lingers in your mind long after the credits roll.

Inside is a short game, but it really sticks with you.

I went into it not knowing much, and honestly that is probably the best way to play it. The game does not explain anything. You are just a boy running through this dark, strange world, and you slowly start realizing that something is very wrong. There is no dialogue, no big story dump, no characters explaining the plot. You just keep moving forward and try to understand the world from what you see.

The atmosphere is easily the best part. Everything feels cold, quiet, and uncomfortable. The forests, factories, labs, underwater parts, and all the strange people you see in the background make the game feel disturbing without trying too hard. It is not really horror in the normal sense, but it has this constant tension that makes you feel unsafe.

The puzzles are simple but well made. They usually do not take too long, but they fit the world nicely. It never feels like the game just placed random puzzles in front of you. Most of the time, solving them feels like you are actually surviving or escaping from something.

Visually, the game is beautiful in a very dark way. The animations, lighting, and small background details are really impressive. It has a simple style, but it looks better than many bigger games because everything feels intentional.

The ending is… weird. Very weird. I am still not completely sure how I feel about it, but I definitely remember it. It is one of those endings where you just sit there for a minute and think, “What the hell did I just play?” But in a good way.

My only warning is that it is pretty short. Do not expect a huge game with lots of content. You can finish it in a few hours. But I would rather play a short game that knows exactly what it wants to be than a long game full of filler.

Inside is simple, dark, strange, and memorable. Definitely worth playing, especially if you like atmospheric games that tell their story without explaining everything.
boring gameplay, good atomsphere, good environment, good music

美工的话我还是很欣赏的，整体画面看起来是偏暗的，可能看起来不太方便，不过很贴合游戏内容，美工还是比较用心的，玩游戏的时候可以明显感觉到一种压抑感，游戏的背景设计的可以说非常好，水鬼可以感觉见恐怖，室外室内都很压抑，不过到了后面主角变成肉球那里我感觉还是有点不适。
音效方面的话可以说非常优秀了，完全贴合环境，与美工共同塑造了压抑的氛围，环境音效非常真实，游戏没有背景音乐，所以玩起来只有游戏内音效。
剧情的话游戏并没有通过文字讲述剧情，而是一步一步让玩家自己推进自己感受剧情，剧情似乎想体现出被操控这一主题，主人公自始至终都处于被控制的局面，无论是逃亡还是肉球都可以发现其他人有在可以引导主人公，最后的结局感觉意外但是合乎情理，男孩到死也没有摆脱控制。我只能理解到这里了，但不妨碍游戏想表达更深层的意思，推荐大家体验一下。
最后说一下，这个游戏全成就不难，不会了可以找攻略，还算比较简单的。

Inside is a puzzle-platformer from Playdead, following a boy's wordless descent from a woods into an ever-deepening facility. The full game was completed through the credits in a single stream.

The sense of scale is the recurring wow, with everything in the world feeling enormous and the boy like an ant within it. The comparison to Little Nightmares is telling, since this world feels a whole other level larger.

The descent narrative keeps delivering, with the facility just continuing through submerged ruins, an overgrown abandoned complex and ever-deeper chambers. The atmosphere is carried by audio, with a distant heartbeat that grows bigger, higher, louder and faster with danger.

The mind-control mechanic is a highlight, with a helmet that lets the boy command the husk-like workers and collect a crew that follows along. The gathered workers help in later sections, making the mechanic feel genuinely useful.

The closing sequences are a memorable payoff, with the game's scale making a strong impression. The ambiguity is acknowledged as a feature, with more questions at the close than at the start.

The narrative stays opaque throughout, with why the boy heads for the facility and what the workers are left unexplained. Some puzzles stump, the movement controls are clumsy, and the dog sections rely on trial and error with tight jump timing.

Overall, the sense of scale, the audio design and the mind-control gimmick make this a cool and mysterious puzzle-platformer. The opaque story and the occasional puzzle stumps are the caveats.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the narrative and ending leave players with many open questions and plenty of room for personal interpretation.

citations.review_text:
As an art piece and an experience, Inside does a great job. It feels like it does exactly what it wants to do and the character animations are very fluid.

As a game? It is the epitome of "mid". Each new mechanic just feels kind of ok, and many of them don't build on each other. It's a game where the gameplay is secondary to the world and story, which is not my cup or tea (but works for some people!). Unfortunately when it comes to the world/story, the game's minimalist approach leaves you with tons of questions. It would be fine if it was just an open-ended ending we're talking about, but the each zone keeps introducing new pieces of world building with zero context that is never provided. 

It just made the whole story feel so arbitrary to me, which made the ending feel less like a culmination of a throughline (e.g. Inception) and more like another arbitrary "ok sure I guess that's it then."

Worth playing if you like games that are more about the world / story than being a game (e.g. What Remains of Edith Finch). But the rating on Steam is deceptive, I do [b]not[/b] think this game is for everyone.

I absolutely loved the suspense and atmosphere in INSIDE. The simple, dark visual design is very distinctive and does an amazing job of creating an unsettling feeling without needing to rely on excessive details or jump scares. There is something about the game's world that constantly makes you feel like something is wrong, and I really enjoyed that.
My only real complaint is about the second ending. Personally, I don't think it's very intuitive to figure out how to obtain it without looking up a guide or tutorial. Maybe I'm just missing something, but I would have preferred a few more subtle hints pointing the player in the right direction.
And speaking of the story... I NEED MORE LORE.
I would genuinely love to see the developers release a DLC or some kind of additional content explaining their creative process and, perhaps even more importantly, giving us a clearer and more complete backstory for this dystopian world.
Yes, there are plenty of things we can infer (experiments, viruses, some kind of strange biological phenomenon, and so on) but the fact that we never get a clear explanation of what is actually happening leaves me with SO many questions.
And honestly? That's probably a testament to how good the game is at creating mystery, because I'm still here wondering what the heck happened.
Simply amazing. They kept the lore as ambiguous as possible so the player can interpret it for him/herself, much like with LIMBO. Still can't get over the OST, so outstanding.

A fantastic game full of atmosphere, amazing art style, cool puzzles and great platforming.

The two endings are the most ambiguous I have ever come across in a video game and what they mean and how you Interpret them are totally up to you. If you like nice little endings all warped up in a bow with everything explained and concluded then pass on this one.

However if you are not a moron that needs everything spoon fed to you then this is one amazing side scrolling platformer, highly recommended.

One of the best indie games I've ever played. Beautiful visuals, amazing sound design. The sound design is so good there are moments where I genuinely felt scared for my life, especially with the dogs. The physics in this game is phenomenal, and every action makes sense once completed. The puzzles in the game are fun, satisfying, and sometimes frustratingly difficult... The ending (s) , and the fact that the leave the interpretation upto us is one of my favourite things about this game. I've replayed this atleast 5times, and I know I will again. 9/10

I still don't fully understand what happened. The atmosphere, sound design, and environmental storytelling are incredible. The ending left me with more questions than answers, and I've been thinking about different theories ever since. If you like games that don't hold your hand and let you figure things out yourself, play this.
I love tp enjoy this type of games. Dark and alone in a different world. But end is not clear yet. I hope there will be second game will continue the the story

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as a linear side-scrolling experience focused on moving forward and escaping dangers.

citations.review_text: You can see influence of Limbo from creator since game is going linear in one direction. Scenes with dog attacks are very disturbing but game is intentionally placing you into those unpleasant environment and situations from the  start. Puzzles are decent, not hard overall but couple of them could made you think what is supposed to be done at the moment, besides this we can all realate to the game story although there are two endings, I got the normal  (recommend to check the other depending on which one do you get). This is peace of art and game should be looked through that perspective, although not my coup of tea it has a huge recommendation.

Inside is a puzzle-platformer from Playdead, following a boy's wordless descent from a woods into an ever-deepening facility. The full game was completed through the credits in a single stream.

The sense of scale is the recurring wow, with everything in the world feeling enormous and the boy like an ant within it. The comparison to Little Nightmares is telling, since this world feels a whole other level larger.

The descent narrative keeps delivering, with the facility just continuing through submerged ruins, an overgrown abandoned complex and ever-deeper chambers. The atmosphere is carried by audio, with a distant heartbeat that grows bigger, higher, louder and faster with danger.

The mind-control mechanic is a highlight, with a helmet that lets the boy command the husk-like workers and collect a crew that follows along. The gathered workers help in later sections, making the mechanic feel genuinely useful.

The closing sequences are a memorable payoff, with the game's scale making a strong impression. The ambiguity is acknowledged as a feature, with more questions at the close than at the start.

The narrative stays opaque throughout, with why the boy heads for the facility and what the workers are left unexplained. Some puzzles stump, the movement controls are clumsy, and the dog sections rely on trial and error with tight jump timing.

Overall, the sense of scale, the audio design and the mind-control gimmick make this a cool and mysterious puzzle-platformer. The opaque story and the occasional puzzle stumps are the caveats.

Inside is a linear platformer with a very unique design and atmosphere.
The controls are very simple but fluid. I like how smooth the transitioning animations are from one action to the other. Stumbling and general feeling of unbalance of the character when he runs and moves, as well as his posture and body language, subtly heightens the feeling of tension and anxiety.
As the story goes it gets increasingly more disturbing and it's unveiled to us without a single word or exposition. Together with the character we get to observe and experience the horrors of this world and try to escape it. The puzzles are not too hard and they are seamlessly incorporated into the scene and feel like a natural part of that world.
The sound design is awesome and the music, when present, never distracts and only adds to the dark ambience.

For me it was a very enjoyable experience and I highly recommend this game for anyone that likes the moody and horror themes in platformer puzzle games.

The game doesn't say much about what you're supposed to do, but the world is very linear and it's all about moving your character forward. There's no magic, no superpowers, nothing that tells you are anything but human; all you have at your fingertips is your smarts, and the abilities to move forward with your own two feet, jump, climb, swim, or push and pull objects. At first everything seems normal, except for the fact that you are running/hiding from someone and getting caught means certain death. But as the chapters progress you encounter weirder and weirder things. The world tethers between post-apocalyptic but also science fiction, and nothing is what it seems.

﻿The black and white world accentuates some of the creepy parts of the game. Even if the game focuses more on shadows and silhouettes, there's still a lot of clarity in the lines and shapes of the world inside the game, so even the various ways you can die are still clear enough.

The animation in the game is pretty good. While it doesn't deal in overly detailed characters, there's a lot of the "small things" in each scene that really gives the game OOMPH. Things like the movement of the lights and shadows may seem like a minor thing, but it vastly affects the gameplay and gaming experience. The backgrounds may not add much because of its 2.5-dimension gameplay, but they add character to the chapters and the scenes. Playdead's backgrounds are amazing artworks on their own that showcase how detail-oriented the developers are.

Like I said, there's not a lot of words but the graphics of the game speaks volumes. And so does the music and sound effects that come at the most apt of times. The music is amazing at building momentum and intrigue where it can jump at you the most.

If you like something that is short but challenging, then INSIDE is a great game to complete. I bought this on a Steam sale so I bought this at a highly discounted price;  so this can be something to watch out for when it goes on sal…

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features zero dialogue, leaving the story and lore entirely open to interpretation without any text or exposition explaining the plot.

citations.review_text: This game was eerie, and even without dialouge the world felt very real and well constructed, especially with how much detail went into the 3D environments.
You don't expect a platformer with literally no dialog to tell such a powerful story...

Inside is just an incredible experience. The animations, the physics, the ambience, the sound, everything, etc. is just so well done. No dialogue and no prompts leave a lot open to interpretation regarding the narrative. I could easily see the theme being related to some sociopolitical commentary just as much as it could be an allegory for internal psychological strife. It’s so good.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the puzzles as straightforward, intuitive, and manageable, though some find them repetitive or occasionally frustrating.

citations.review_text:
A truly gorgeous experience that is more a piece of art than anything else.

The game focuses around some pretty simple mechanics that require little time to master. Most of my brain usage went towards exploration and solving the puzzles, which were overall quite intuitive and didn't keep me stuck for more than a few minutes at a time (if that).

Though the ability to explore the environment lent a lot to the game, what I feel makes this truly stand out is the artistic and sonic direction. The way the environment comes into and out of view offers a beautifully dynamic look into the world that the Boy is trying to escape: as the camera moves in a truly gorgeous, fluid, and cinematic fashion through each new space, different elements flit into and out of focus, cleverly shifting our perspective and changing how much we see. I felt this was a very strong choice that lent wonderfully-fitting somber grace to the atmosphere. Beyond that, the design of each new area felt very artful and immersive. Many areas I loved -- the forest, beach, cornfields -- and some I hated -- hello, abjectly disturbing Mine region (that one [i]really[/i] got to me for some reason -- but regardless of my response to each environment, every single one served a purpose in fleshing out the Boy's world without detracting from it whatsoever. That can be quite difficult to do, I feel.

On top of that, as the physical environments changed and varied, so did the sonic landscapes. Some of the transitions between areas were truly awe-inspiring and forced me to pause for a moment so I could fully take in the shift. It helps a lot that the sound design is very complete, detailed, and tasteful. This is particularly obvious when you move between dry land and the underwater landscape. In my opinion, it brought volumes (ha) to the experience.

A final note on what I loved: how much you learn about the world just through visual storytelling. There is no dialogue and no written lore on scraps of documents. A lot …
Super fun and unique game. A good challenge without being super difficult.

Having played through the game and read reviews, I cannot for the life of me understand why INSIDE is rated so highly.

The art and sound design are exceptional, and the mechanics are excellent as well - for example, swinging close to water on a rope leaves ripples; animations play fluidly and feel alive, but there's a reason the publisher markets it purely based off of awards for atmosphere and art.

The puzzles.
Oh man. the 'puzzles'. 
I understand the limitations of a side-scrolling game where a character can only push/pull objects, but do you REALLY need to repeat the same puzzles?
 
[go to the right of the screen - find an obstacle - go back to the left of the screen - find a box - drag box to the right of the screen] 
[go right - wait - go right] 
[go right - push button - go right]
[go right and do something - go back left to pull the enemies away - go right and do something]

INSIDE is more of a walking simulator than a puzzle game, which I wouldn't mind at all if the puzzles themselves weren't so tedious. All two hours of gameplay are filled with these exact same puzzles over and over again, with only the background art and models differentiating them. The most interesting puzzle, pretending to blend in with the other puppets, is a mechanic present in one sequence near the start of the game and promptly discarded. They snatched defeat from the jaws of victory in the most boring way possible.

But what of it's story? Well my friend, get ready for the most milquetoast commentary on power, agency and societal control that I have ever seen. Ten years of radio silence by the developers is truly awful, and I do feel for the fanbase picking up scraps and tying together theories that i'm certain are thousands of times better than anything envisioned by the developers.

INSIDE is a terrifically meh puzzle game held up by it's art direction. 3/10

Got this gem for around 3 US dollars. Worth the full price tag without discount.

The only complaint I have is how long it takes to move to different locations throughout the experience.

That being said... This is amazingly done. The puzzles are not too complex yet not too simple. Often you will find yourself saying "[I]Oh, I'm dumb, that makes sense.[/i]"

The atmosphere of the game looks incredible, despite having low recommended specs. Terrifying yet beautiful.

INSIDE kept surprising me... It's rich amount of mechanics, it's unsettling deaths and surroundings, are a few such ways.

8.5/10 I do [b]recommend[/b].
Great game, marked the start of one true 2d horror, great storyline and the puzzles were just the right amount of challenge. Would definitely recommend.

A beautiful game, with a few hickups here and there, is what I'd use to describe this one. Having played through Limbo and coming to this one, the color and vibrance was a welcome shift in tone, but what didn't change was the mystery involved within. We don't really know what we've got ourselves into until the second half of the story and it was quite gripping from start to finish. The puzzles, while not as hard as Limbos were quite well done for the most part, except the tedious water levels that weren't that great. As a package though, it provides a great ending to the whole thing and the final few moments left me feeling melancholic of the things we saw and endured, through the eyes of the boy. Highly recommend it. 
9/10.
Amazing story and visuals, puzzles are fun but sometimes too easy. Definitely worth a buy
the start and halfway was fun because it had more action than puzzle but after that it was all confusing puzzles which wasnt really fun still i would give this game a positive review

Good puzzle game, have 100%ed the achievements on many platforms now at this point. It’s definitely worth playing and a very pretty game. I like LIMBO just a little bit more but still a satisfying puzzler with a good atmosphere.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the controls are simple and responsive, featuring fluid character animations and interactions.

citations.review_text:
As an art piece and an experience, Inside does a great job. It feels like it does exactly what it wants to do and the character animations are very fluid.

As a game? It is the epitome of "mid". Each new mechanic just feels kind of ok, and many of them don't build on each other. It's a game where the gameplay is secondary to the world and story, which is not my cup or tea (but works for some people!). Unfortunately when it comes to the world/story, the game's minimalist approach leaves you with tons of questions. It would be fine if it was just an open-ended ending we're talking about, but the each zone keeps introducing new pieces of world building with zero context that is never provided. 

It just made the whole story feel so arbitrary to me, which made the ending feel less like a culmination of a throughline (e.g. Inception) and more like another arbitrary "ok sure I guess that's it then."

Worth playing if you like games that are more about the world / story than being a game (e.g. What Remains of Edith Finch). But the rating on Steam is deceptive, I do [b]not[/b] think this game is for everyone.

Playdead combined logic and horror into a phenomenal puzzle-platformer that will have you hooked until you finished it. The game isn't overcomplicated, only needing WASD and a few other keys to run through the storyline. While it isn't overcomplicated, it can definitely be challenging by presenting you with puzzles relying solely on logic and timing. INSIDE also leaves a lot of room for interpretation, with things happening that will really make you stop and think, "What did I just watch?" You need to play it for yourself to see what theories you come up with.

[h1]Review[/h1]
What did I just play? The game launches with no menu, no introduction, no UI elements. Just a boy on the screen who reacts to the controls, and I got moving. The controls themselves are super smooth and intuitive. No fuss, no need for hints; they were just where you expected them to be. The mysterious atmosphere that started this entire experience persisted, and the curiosity about what was going on pulled me back in between sessions. Unexpectedly sombre but beautiful. Was confused at first, but then things made a lot more sense (I still have a lot of questions). Melancholic but mighty, this was a pleasant experience.

Note: The IK and animations fluidly interacting with the controls was real nice.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game launches directly into gameplay with no introductory menus, tutorial prompts, or user interface elements on screen.

citations.review_text:
In an ocean of overbearing tutorials, blinking UI elements calling for attention, replay incentives, seasonal events, progress bars to fill out, scores to beat, weekly quests, daily login rewards, and so many more features trying to control our gaming time... [i]it is such a relief to be left alone in peace to figure out a game.[/i] 

Inside never tells you what to do. It can't be grinded. It doesn't have a shop. 

What it has is a start, an end and a 4-hour single player adventure in-between. A story that isn't told but shown. A gameplay that is so well designed that it comes free of any interface, tutorial or difficulty settings. 

The main character dies a hundred horrible deaths in a sick world, but damn it's a great video game!

Absolutely fantastic game. I really hate all the chatgpt reviews on steam because, especially for amazing games like this one, they say the most cliche ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ instead of actually saying what makes the game great. The actual things that make the game great are these; The atmosphere pulls you in completely, the story somehow is insanely engaging without a single word spoken, you're constantly asking yourself "what the hell is all this", the game basically strikes you with awe at every turn, and it ends with a weirdly simple but beautiful ending. It doesn't hold your hand ever, it doesn't explain anything, it's just you and the game, and it's perfect.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the controls as simple and intuitive, relying on basic movement keys and a minimal set of inputs.

citations.review_text:
Now this is a game! 11/10 score for me. In a lot of ways, its easily one of the best games I've ever played and I wouldn't be surprised If it is at the somewhere at top of ALL time list of games. I'm not joking

The story is fantastic (don't ask me what its about though), the atmosphere/design is beautiful, the pacing is wonderful, the puzzles are sensible, very simple controls but the context of the level makes it feel like so much more than that. In fact it is so simple that it would make a good first game to introduce someone -anyone really - to gaming. 

Thank you PLAYDEAD!
